newsitem.title: UK: British bookmaker in about-turn on Dunblane record.
newsitem.headline: British bookmaker in about-turn on Dunblane record.

text.p: A British bookmaker on Saturday tipped a recording by the people of Dunblane as a Christmas pop chart hit and then cancelled betting after deciding the gamble was in bad taste.

William Hill takes bets each year on which record will be number one in the pop charts on December 25. But it said it did not want to be seen making money out of a record by people from the Scottish town where 16 schoolchildren and their teacher were shot dead by a crazed gunman in March.
"This is a one-off situation and it is just so different from anything else. We did not want to be seen to be making money out of tragic circumstances," said a William Hill spokesman.
Only a few hours earlier, the bookmaker had offered odds of five-to-one on the record being the Christmas hit.

The song, a version of Bob Dylan's "Knocking on Heaven's Door" is yet to be recorded. It is reportedly being made as part of the townspeople's campaign for a ban on private ownership of handguns and is said to have the approval of victims' parents.
